paper.title_en: Triangular and fourth-order flow of D mesons in Pb-Pb collisions with event-by-event fluctuations
paper.abstract_en: Charm quarks are valuable probes of the transport properties of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP), yet the role of event-by-event medium fluctuations in shaping their observables remains to be quantified. We study this problem in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.02$~TeV by coupling the iEBE-VISHNU event-by-event viscous hydrodynamic framework to a Langevin transport model with instantaneous coalescence hadronization. We find that fluctuations have little effect on the azimuthally averaged $D$ meson nuclear modification factor $R_{AA}$, which remains close to the smooth-background baseline with only modest momentum-dependent deviations. In contrast, the anisotropic flow coefficients $v_n$ are increasingly sensitive to fluctuations with rising harmonic order $n$. In particular, the triangular flow $v_3$, which vanishes in the smooth background, is entirely generated by initial-state fluctuations, and our results reproduce the main features of the available CMS measurements. We further present predictions for the $D$ meson $v_4$, which provide a quantitative benchmark for future measurements of higher-order heavy-flavor flow and help elucidate the interplay between event-by-event QGP fluctuations and charm quark dynamics.
